newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks close slightly down, Eurotunnel up.
newsitem.headline: French stocks close slightly down, Eurotunnel up.

text.p: French shares closed slightly down on prolonged profit-taking and a lower Wall Street after two stronger-than-expected U.S. economic reports, dealers said.

The French truckers' strike is worrying mainly foreign investments but negotiations resumed in the afternoon between striking French truck drivers and employers and ministers expressed optimism that an agreement in the 10-day-old dispute that has choked French highways could be reached within hours.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was down 4.31 points or 0.19 percent at 2,270.77 at while the CAC-40 futures contract was down at 2,274 from 2,276 on Tuesday's close.
An upward revision of the third quarter U.S. GDP figure and strong October durable goods figures rekindled some inflation fears and pushed U.S. stocks down and French shares as well.

"I think that the consolidation will continue until the CAC-40 is at 2,220/30 but this will be followed by an attack on the important resistance level of 2,290 before the end of the year," said a technical analyst at brokers Transbourse.
* Volume was 5.6 billion francs, of which 4.2 billion was in blue-chip shares due to a raft of basket deals ahead of the expiry of the November CAC-40 futures contract, dealers said.

* Eurotunnel closed 9.3 percent higher at 7.05 francs as most active stock on speculative buying after a week of declines. The rise followed statements by company officials downplaying the financial impact of the November 18 truck fire which gutted a tunnel section.

* UAP, the second most active stock, closed 0.43 percent lower at 138.50 francs in continued arbitrage with AXA, down 0.38 percent at 311.20 francs. The European Commission said on Wednesday it was starting a preliminary probe into the proposed merger deal.

* Alcatel Alsthom fell 0.35 percent to 460.50 after comments by chairman Serge Tchuruk were published saying the company was ready to make a fresh bid for Thomson when the Lagardere bid's validity expires on December 31. "It creates a new uncertainty and investors do not like that," a dealer said.
* Sanofi up 2.04 percent after an analysts briefing on Tuesday on new drugs in the beauty products sector.
* Elf slips 1.21 percent to 449 francs, after earlier advances on a higher nine-month sales figure.
* M6 falls 2.41 percent to 446 francs after broker Cheuvreux de Virieu turned negative and issued a sell notice.
* Air Liquide up 1.27 percent at 796 francs. Brokerage Dupont-denant upgraded recommendation to "market perfomer" and increased profit forecasts.
* Cerus up 2.44 percent at 126 francs on a report it would sell 48.05 percent of Cofir in Spain for 700 million francs. Cerus was not available for comment.

* Saint-Gobain slips 0.14 percent to 724 francs as the European Commission confirmed earlier reports it was blocking a merger plan between the silicon carbide interests of the French group, Germany's Waecker-Chimie and Dutch state-owned investment firm NOM.
* Carrefour ends 0.06 percent higher at 3,182 after having hit a year high of 3,199 francs during the day.

* Bull suspended pending capital increase. France Telecom, Motorola and NEC to increase their stakes to just below 20 percent respectively from 17 percent. State reducing its stake to 30 percent from 30 percent.

* Renault, down 0.76 percent at 118.01 francs, said it is in talks to establish a possible venture to assemble Megane cars at the Moscow-owned Moskvitch plant and sell them in Russia, but no agreement has been struck yet.
